text: does the grammatically plural Hebrew word Elohim mean God or Gods hey everybody I'm Dan mclen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion and the answer is
yes it can mean either one and the easiest way to tell is to just look at the verbs the participles and the pronouns that are associated with the
noun and if they are singular then that noun is being used singularly if they are plural then that noun means gods in
the plural it can also be used adjectivally to mean Divine it is not a plural of majesty it is not the Royal we
there's no analog in English for what was going on anciently in these Semitic languages the best argument for what's
going on I think is Joel Brett's 2001 book a reassessment of biblical Elohim where he argues that it is probably a
concretized abstract plural and if you'd like more details on that you can check out his book another way that it is not
being used is as an honorific reference to judges or other people with authority when the Hebrew Bible uses the word
Elohim it is referring to things that are Divine and if it is used in reference to humans then the Hebrew Bible is designating those humans as
Divine and there was overlap between the two and I discuss that in some detail in my own book adoniz Divine Images a
